$comment: Source of truth for iterated work. ./scripts/seed-issues.sh creates milestones and issues from this file; it is idempotent on exact title. See docs/iterations/README.md.

milestones.title: iteration-00: settle decisions
milestones.description: Resolve the open questions in docs/grill/brief.md before building. Done when every question is an ADR or an explicit deferral with a trigger.

milestones.title: iteration-01: phase 0 bootstrap
milestones.description: Execute docs/plans/0001-phase-0-bootstrap.md. Done when one Oracle A1 node in Canada runs the Compose stack, the tracker is live, and a rebuild drill has passed.

milestones.title: iteration-02: optional ROG worker
milestones.description: Onboard the ROG Strix G16 as an optional worker under the ADR-0002 contract. Optional: this milestone never gates a retro, and the platform must work with the machine switched off.

issues.title: Q1: settle the Oracle home region (Toronto vs Montreal)
issues.summary: The OCI home region is permanent and Always Free compute must run there, so this is decided once at signup. Both Canadian regions have a single availability domain; A1 capacity is the real constraint, not features.
acceptance: A1 capacity checked in ca-toronto-1 and ca-montreal-1 before creating the account
Home region chosen, recorded in the password manager, and not derived from a second account
ADR-0001 updated with the chosen region and its rationale
docs/grill/brief.md Q1 marked resolved

issues.title: Q2: confirm Postgres in Docker as the Phase 1 database
issues.summary: Postgres in a container with nightly dumps versus a managed free tier (Neon, Supabase) versus SQLite for small sites. A managed tier adds a network hop, cold starts, and a second vendor.
acceptance: Database choice recorded as an ADR
RPO/RTO targets consistent with the backup policy in Q11
The trigger for moving to managed Postgres is written down

issues.title: Q3: choose what runs the scheduler
issues.summary: Host cron, Ofelia labels, an app-level scheduler, or GitHub Actions schedules. The deciding constraint is that every job must feed an external dead-man's switch.
acceptance: Scheduler choice recorded in an ADR or in the plan
Every scheduled job has a spelled-out Healthchecks.io ping path
GitHub Actions is explicitly ruled in or out as a scheduler

issues.title: Q4: choose the queue for triggered jobs
issues.summary: A Postgres-backed queue (SKIP LOCKED, pg-boss, Procrastinate) versus Redis plus a worker library versus a cloud queue. Fewer stateful services keeps the backup story to one database.
acceptance: Queue choice recorded, with the throughput ceiling that would force a change
Queue state included in the backup and restore drill
Failure and retry semantics documented

issues.title: Q5: fix the observability stack
issues.summary: A light on-box stack (Dozzle, Uptime Kuma, Healthchecks.io, Sentry) versus a centralized free tier (Grafana Cloud). At least one check must live off the host that it monitors.
acceptance: Logs, uptime, errors, and metrics each have exactly one named tool
Every public endpoint and every scheduled job has an external check
The trigger for moving to a centralized log store is written down
Alert routing matches docs/integrations/issue-tracker.md

issues.title: Q6: settle the deploy and rollback procedure
issues.summary: GitHub Actions over Tailscale into deploy.sh, Watchtower, a GitOps agent, or manual pulls. The important parts are immutable image tags by SHA, a kept previous tag, and migrations as a separate gated step.
acceptance: Deploy path and rollback command recorded in docs/runbooks/
Images are referenced by commit SHA, not latest
Migrations run only after a backup and have a written reverse path
A rollback is rehearsed as part of iteration-01 task 11

issues.title: Q7: settle where secrets live
issues.summary: A mode-600 .env on the host plus GitHub Secrets, versus SOPS/age in the repo, versus a managed secret store. The migration trigger is a second operator or a client handover.
acceptance: Secret locations documented, with who can read each one
Rotation procedure written for SSH keys, database password, Telegram token, and restic password
The trigger for moving to SOPS or a secret store is recorded

issues.title: Q8: decide whether Phase 1 has staging
issues.summary: 12 GB does not comfortably hold two full stacks. The realistic options are local Compose, a second Compose project with its own database, or no staging at all.
acceptance: Decision recorded with the memory budget that supports it
The condition that forces staging (first client review) is written down

issues.title: Q9: define client isolation
issues.summary: One Compose project per client with its own database and user, a shared app with tenant schemas, or one host per client. Requires deciding the maximum number of clients per host.
acceptance: Isolation model recorded, including the shared components (Caddy, host)
Per-client naming convention for database, user, subdomain, and labels
A client-count ceiling per host is stated

issues.title: Q10: choose the ingress path (A record, proxy, or Tunnel)
issues.summary: Direct A record with Caddy, Cloudflare proxy in front of Caddy, or Cloudflare Tunnel with no inbound ports. Each changes the firewall, the failure modes, and what is visible to the provider.
acceptance: Ingress path recorded with the firewall rules it implies
Origin exposure and certificate handling documented
The condition that would move to Tunnel is written down

issues.title: Q11: approve the backup and restore policy
issues.summary: Nightly pg_dump plus restic, versus WAL archiving, versus managed PITR. Also fixes the retention set, the RPO/RTO claim, and the drill cadence.
acceptance: Retention, RPO, RTO, and drill cadence agreed and written down
The claim is honest for the chosen method, not aspirational
docs/runbooks/restore.md reflects the agreed policy

issues.title: Q12: define the triggers for moving off Oracle
issues.summary: Move when evidence says so, not on a fixed date. Candidate triggers include sustained CPU or memory pressure, a client SLA, a second stateful client database, egress above 1 TB per month, or repeated capacity and reclamation incidents.
acceptance: Numeric triggers recorded in an ADR
A provider free-tier change is named as an immediate trigger
The default target (paid VPS with the same Compose file) is stated

issues.title: Q13: adopt the security baseline
issues.summary: UFW default deny, 80/443 only, SSH closed after Tailscale works, unattended upgrades, Cloudflare proxy in front, no root containers where avoidable, Sentry PII scrubbing.
acceptance: Baseline written as a checklist in the runbooks
Port 22 closure is part of the rebuild runbook, not a manual afterthought
The compliance trigger for adding SSO or audit logs is recorded

issues.title: Q14: choose the domain strategy
issues.summary: A free subdomain, a cheap .dev or .ca domain at cost, or waiting until the first client. A domain is the only likely Phase 1 expense.
acceptance: Decision recorded, including whether Phase 0 buys a domain
DNS TTL and migration practice documented

issues.title: Q15: publish the explicit non-goals list
issues.summary: No Kubernetes, Nomad, k3s, multi-region, custom PaaS, GPU worker, Windows, Android emulator, or self-service portal. Revisiting any of these needs an ADR and a measured need.
acceptance: Non-goals appear in README.md and docs/requirements.md
Each non-goal names the condition that would reopen it

issues.title: Q17: decide what role, if any, the ROG plays
issues.summary: The ROG Strix G16 is expected to become reachable around 2026-12-06. ADR-0002 already limits it to an optional worker; the open part is which role, and on what runtime. Windows plus WSL2 is acceptable; dual boot is not.
acceptance: Role chosen from the table in docs/workers/rog-g16.md, or the machine is left unused
Runtime decided: Windows plus WSL2, or a single-boot Linux install if it is ever promoted
Owner agreement on what may run and when is recorded
ADR-0002 confirmed or amended to match the choice

issues.title: T1: create the Oracle tenancy and record its identifiers
issues.summary: Create exactly one Oracle account with the home region chosen in Q1, enable MFA, and record the tenancy and compartment OCIDs in the password manager.
acceptance: Availability checked in ca-toronto-1 and ca-montreal-1 before signup
One account created with the chosen home region, MFA enabled
Tenancy OCID, compartment OCID, and region stored in the password manager
Always Free limits visible in the console

issues.title: T2: provision the A1 instance with Terraform
issues.summary: Apply infra/oracle: VCN, public subnet, internet gateway, route table, security list, and one VM.Standard.A1.Flex at 2 OCPU / 12 GB with a 100 GB boot volume and reserved public IP.
acceptance: terraform apply completes in the chosen region
ssh works with the bootstrap key
nproc reports 2 and free -g reports about 12 GB
Public IP recorded and DNS plan noted

issues.title: T3: harden the host
issues.summary: Create the deploy user, disable password and root SSH, enable UFW with 22/80/443, install fail2ban, enable unattended upgrades, add 2 GB swap, and set the timezone to America/Toronto.
acceptance: A second SSH session works as the deploy user
ufw status shows only the intended rules
Password authentication and root login are disabled
swapon --show reports 2 GB

issues.title: T4: join Tailscale and close public SSH
issues.summary: Join the tailnet with a single-use tagged auth key, confirm MagicDNS, verify Tailscale SSH, then remove the public port 22 rule from the security list and UFW.
acceptance: tailscale status shows the node online with MagicDNS resolving
ssh over Tailscale works after port 22 is closed publicly
External port 22 scan fails
Single-use auth key revoked

issues.title: T5: install Docker and start the Compose stack
issues.summary: Install Docker Engine and the Compose plugin, clone the repo to /srv/dev-platform, create a mode-600 .env, and start compose/compose.yaml.
acceptance: docker compose ps shows healthy services
curl -I http://localhost:80 returns 200 on the host
Postgres accepts connections on the Compose network
.env is mode 600 and gitignored

issues.title: T6: wire DNS, TLS, and the first public service
issues.summary: Point the chosen domain at the Oracle public IP through Cloudflare, set DOMAIN in .env, and confirm Caddy issues a valid certificate and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
acceptance: curl -I https://<domain> returns 200 with a valid certificate
HTTP redirects to HTTPS
SSL Labs grade A or better
status.<domain> and logs.<domain> have records if they are kept

issues.title: T7: ship one static site on Cloudflare Pages
issues.summary: Create a Pages project, attach a domain, and prove both a deploy and a rollback without touching the Oracle node.
acceptance: The site loads over HTTPS
A rollback to the previous deployment works
The site still loads with the Oracle node stopped

issues.title: T8: run one scheduled job behind a dead-man's switch
issues.summary: Add one scheduled job, make it do real work and ping Healthchecks.io on success, then stop it deliberately and confirm the alert arrives.
acceptance: The job runs on schedule and writes visible output
Healthchecks.io reports the ping
Stopping the job produces an email alert within the grace period
Alert routing matches docs/integrations/issue-tracker.md

issues.title: T9: nightly encrypted backups to object storage
issues.summary: Create the OCI Object Storage bucket and S3-compatible key, configure restic, run scripts/backup.sh, schedule it nightly, and ping Healthchecks.io on success and failure.
acceptance: A snapshot exists in object storage
restic check passes
The job is scheduled and pings on both outcomes
Retention matches the policy agreed in Q11

issues.title: T10: pass the restore drill
issues.summary: Restore the latest dump into a scratch database, compare a row count and checksum with production, then run the real restore path and record the time.
acceptance: Scratch restore completes and matches production on a row count and a checksum
scripts/restore.sh completes end to end
Time taken recorded in docs/runbooks/restore.md
Restore finishes in under 15 minutes

issues.title: T11: CI builds a multi-arch image and deploys over Tailscale
issues.summary: Add a workflow that builds linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, pushes to GHCR by commit SHA, and a deploy job that SSHes over Tailscale and runs scripts/deploy.sh.
acceptance: A push to main produces a tagged multi-arch image
The deploy job runs deploy.sh on the node and passes the health check
Rolling back to the previous SHA takes one command
No long-lived SSH key is stored where a rotation cannot reach it

issues.title: T12: external monitoring and alerting
issues.summary: Add an external uptime check, a TLS expiry check, a disk-space alert at 80%, a budget alert, and Sentry for application errors. Prove each one fires.
acceptance: Each check fires in a deliberate test
Disk and budget alerts reach a channel that is read daily
Sentry is installed and scrubs PII
Monitor list documented in docs/architecture.md

issues.title: T13: pass the rebuild drill
issues.summary: Destroy the instance while keeping a boot volume snapshot, rebuild from infra/oracle plus cloud-init plus Compose, restore the database, and confirm service.
acceptance: End-to-end rebuild completes in under 30 minutes
The service is healthy afterwards and DNS is correct
Measured time recorded in docs/runbooks/rebuild.md
No manual step is missing from the runbook

issues.title: T14: make the issue tracker live end to end
issues.summary: Labels, templates, the project board, Telegram notifications, and Sentry plus CI intake all working, with one message per event.
acceptance: Labels created and templates apply the right ones
A new issue produces exactly one Telegram message
A CI failure opens or comments on exactly one source:ci issue
A Sentry error creates or links one issue
Triage happens weekly against the Triage view

issues.title: T15: decide the next phase
issues.summary: After 30 days of real use, review cost, capacity, and incidents, then decide whether to stay free, add a warm standby, or move to PAYG or a paid VPS.
acceptance: 30 days of capacity, cost, and incident data reviewed
Decision recorded as an ADR
STRATEGY.md phase table updated

issues.title: X1: create the GitHub Project board and its views
issues.summary: The gh token lacks the project scope, so this is a browser task. Create one Project over dev-platform with the Status, Priority, Source, Client, and Repo fields and the five saved views from the integration doc.
acceptance: One Project exists and is linked to this repository
Fields match docs/integrations/issue-tracker.md
Five views exist: My queue, Triage, CI failures, Client work, Roadmap
New issues land in the project automatically

issues.title: X2: prove the tracker escape hatch works
issues.summary: ADR-0005 makes the FOSS exit a hard requirement. Run scripts/export-issues.sh, import the export into a throwaway GitLab or Forgejo project, and confirm that titles, bodies, states, labels, milestones, and original issue numbers survive.
acceptance: Export runs and produces issues, labels, and milestones JSON
A throwaway GitLab or Forgejo project imports every issue with its original number recorded in the body
Label and milestone mapping is documented, including the gaps
Time to complete a tracker-only migration is recorded in docs/integrations/issue-tracker.md

issues.title: R1: onboard the ROG as a remote Docker builder
issues.summary: When the machine is reachable, join it to the tailnet as tag:worker, run buildkitd inside WSL2, and register it with docker buildx. No unique state, no inbound ports, no place on the merge path.
acceptance: Tailscale ACL blocks 22 and 5432 from the worker to the primary
Buildkit is reachable over Tailscale as a remote builder
One representative multi-arch build measured with and without it
The role is kept only if the time saving is real
docs/architecture.md shows it as a dashed optional node

issues.title: R2: prove the platform has no dependency on the ROG
issues.summary: The ADR-0002 contract is only real if it is tested. With the ROG powered off or removed from the tailnet, the platform must still build, deploy, run jobs, and back up.
acceptance: make check passes with the ROG off
A deploy from a clean clone succeeds with the ROG off
One scheduled job and one backup run succeed with the ROG off
Any step that failed has been fixed, not waived
Result recorded in the issue and linked from ADR-0002

issues.title: R3: decide whether the ROG ever becomes a second Compose host
issues.summary: Promoting the ROG to a host would add client-isolation or warm-standby capacity at $0, but it can disappear without notice. That trade needs an ADR before any state lands on it.
acceptance: Decision recorded as an ADR, including the state it would hold
If promoted: a backup and restore path exists for that state
If rejected: the condition that would reopen it is written down
